question: How Do I Choose the Right Payment Gateway for a New Store?
metaDescription: Start from where your customers actually are and what you sell — fees matter, but a mismatched gateway costs far more in lost conversion than in rate.
shortAnswer: Start from the customer base and product type rather than the fee schedule alone: which country are most customers in (this affects both supported currencies and which local payment methods matter), is the business model one-time purchases or something needing recurring billing, and does the product category fall into anything a gateway restricts. Fees matter too, but a gateway mismatched to the actual customer base costs far more in lost conversion than a slightly higher processing rate ever will.

bodyHtml:
Start With These Questions, Not the Fee Schedule

It's tempting to compare gateways purely on their headline transaction rate, but the rate difference between major providers is usually small compared to the cost of choosing one that doesn't fit the store's actual needs — a gateway that doesn't support a key local payment method, or can't handle recurring billing a business model needs later, causes far more damage than an extra fraction of a percent per transaction.

Key Factors to Weigh

  • Where the customer base actually is — this determines both currency settlement support and whether region-specific local payment methods (iDEAL, Bancontact, and similar) are worth having available from day one.
  • Whether the business model needs recurring billing, even if not immediately — choosing a gateway with solid subscription support upfront avoids a painful migration later if the store adds a subscription product down the line.
  • Product category restrictions some gateways enforce (certain supplements, adult content, high-risk categories) that could block approval entirely regardless of how good the rate looks on paper.
  • Ease of integration and support quality matter more for a new, smaller store without in-house development resources — a well-documented, widely used gateway with strong WooCommerce-specific support tends to cause fewer headaches than a newer, less common option.
  • Actual fee structure, read carefully, including currency conversion handling and payout timing, once the above factors have narrowed the realistic options down to a shortlist.

A Practical Approach

  1. Map out the customer base, product type, and any known future plans (subscriptions, international expansion) before comparing anything.
  2. Shortlist 2-3 gateways that clearly fit those requirements, rather than starting from a long list of every option available.
  3. Compare fee structures and support quality within that shortlist, using the full picture (currency conversion, payout timing, dispute fees) rather than just the headline rate.
  4. Set up a second gateway as a backup from the start where practical, rather than treating multi-gateway as an afterthought.
